ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm just assuming, but I guess this conversation does involve me."

rows.jp: 「美希ちんもナイフとか持ってたろ？　あれは捨てた方がいいかな」
rows.en: “You had a knife too, didn't you, Miki-kins? Think you ought to get rid of it?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You have a knife too, Miki-chin, right? I'd throw that away if I were you."
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「便利なんですけどねぇ、あると」

ghs.en: Miki: "But it's so useful to have, you know."

rows.jp: 「ナイフなんて持ってたんだ？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Why do you even have a knife?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri merely asks in surprise whether Miki had a knife. The English adds a demand for the reason and the emphatic judgment 'even.'

highlights.text: Why do you even have a knife?

rows.jp: 「にゃー」

ghs.en: Miki: "Meeeow."

rows.jp: 「あ、ごめん」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Ah, sorry."

rows.jp: 「すげー便利だなあ、それ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That thing's reeeally useful, yes."

rows.jp: どういう文法なんだろう。
rows.en: What kind of grammar did it use?

ghs.en: What sort of grammar could it even have.

rows.jp: 「日常のありとあらゆる場面で活躍しますよ」

ghs.en: Miki: "Useful in every single possible scene of daily life."

rows.jp: 「……うーん、まあ霧ちんに渡したりしなければいいんでない？」
rows.en: “...Well, as long as you don't hand it over to Kiri-kins, I guess it's fine.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...oookay, so, well, if you don't give it over to Kiri you should be OK I guess?"
ghs.assessment: The diminutive address 霧ちん is reduced to the bare name, removing the marked familiarity.

rows.jp: 「はい。ではそのように」

ghs.en: Miki: "Yes. That is how it'll be."

rows.jp: 「いやー、しかし霧ちんとせんぱいが和解とは……世も末ですね」
rows.en: “Still, Kiri-kins and Taichi making peace... It really is the end of the world.”

ghs.en: Miki: "But ooooh, Kiri-chin and Senpai have made up... it's the end of the world it is."
ghs.assessment: Both Japanese forms of address are carried over rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: 「和解したわけでは」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Well, made up, it's that..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri starts to deny that they have reconciled. The English is ungrammatical and does not express that negation.

rows.jp: 「……だそうで」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...we totally did."
ghs.assessment: Taichi reports Kiri's unfinished denial with 'so she says.' The English instead makes him affirm that they reconciled, reversing both content and attribution.

rows.jp: 「ふーむ」

ghs.en: Miki: "Uhhh-huh."

rows.jp: 「先輩、ちとこちらに」

ghs.en: Miki: "Senpai, this way for a bit."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 手を引かれ、アンテナから離れていく。
rows.en: She took my hand and led me away from the antenna.

ghs.en: Pulling my hand, she moves us away from the antenna,
ghs.assessment: Miki takes Taichi by the hand and leads him away. The dangling participle makes her pull Taichi's hand as though it were her own action object and the vague 'moves us' obscures who leads whom.

highlights.text: Pulling my hand, she moves us

rows.jp: 会話が霧たちに届かない位置。
rows.en: She stopped where Kiri and Misato couldn't hear us.

ghs.en: to a position where we can't be heard by Kiri or Senpai.
ghs.assessment: 霧たち means Kiri and the others, not an alternative between Kiri and an untranslated senior title.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...whassit?"

rows.jp: 「だいたいの事情は聞きましたけど」

ghs.en: Miki: "I've heard the general outline, but,"

rows.jp: あの猫語、すごいな。

ghs.en: That Catspeak's amazing.

rows.jp: 「先輩の方は、それでいいんですか？」

ghs.en: Miki: "Senpai, on your part, are you OK with this?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「いいとは？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "'OK', meaning...?"

rows.jp: 美希の疑問が、よくわからない。
rows.en: I did not understand the question.

ghs.en: I don't quite get Miki's question.

rows.jp: 「確かに霧ちんは、先輩のことちょっぴりその……苦手みたいで……」
rows.en: “Kiri-kins is a little... uncomfortable around you...”

ghs.en: Miki: "Of course Kiri-chin sees you just a bit... as not entirely nice, Senpai..."
ghs.assessment: 苦手 means Kiri is uncomfortable with or has trouble dealing with him, not that she judges him 'not entirely nice'; both Japanese address forms also remain untranslated.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin sees you just a bit... as not entirely nice, Senpai

rows.jp: 「嫌ってたよ。はっきり言って」
rows.en: “She hated me. You can say it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She hates me. Just say that plainly."
ghs.assessment: 嫌ってた is retrospective: she hated or had disliked him. The English changes it to an unqualified present state.

rows.jp: 「あはは……まあ」

ghs.en: Miki: "Ahahah... well."

rows.jp: 苦笑い。

ghs.en: Bitter smile.
ghs.assessment: 苦笑い is a wry or awkward smile, not necessarily an expression of bitterness.

rows.jp: 「実は、二人だけでみんなと離れて暮らそうって誘われていたんです」
rows.en: “Actually, she asked me to go off and live apart from everyone, just the two of us.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Truth is, she invited me to live together with her, just the two of us, away from everyone."

rows.jp: 「え、どうして？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eh, but why?"

rows.jp: 「霧っち、人間不信なんですよ。で、こういう無秩序な状況になったら、先輩みたいな人のそばにいるのは危険だって言うです」
rows.en: “Kiri doesn't trust people. She says that with everything lawless like this, it's dangerous to stay near someone like you.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Kiricchi doesn't trust humans, that's why. And with things have gotten this chaotic, she says it's dangerous to stay next to people like you, Senpai."
ghs.assessment: The clause is missing a conjunction or finite framing, and the two marked Japanese address forms remain untranslated.

highlights.text: with things have gotten this chaotic

rows.jp: いやー、良い眼力だ、霧ちん。

ghs.en: Wooow, nice insight, Kiri-chin.
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「だから……そのぅ……先輩のことをですね」

ghs.en: Miki: "That's why... well... her and you, Senpai."
ghs.assessment: Miki hesitantly raises Kiri's view of Taichi. The English is a sentence fragment with an object pronoun, gives no coherent proposition, and retains the Japanese title.

rows.jp: 「仮想敵国にしていたと」

ghs.en: Taichi: "On how she sees me as a hypothetical enemy government."
ghs.assessment: 仮想敵国 is a hypothetical enemy state or nation, not an enemy government.

ghs.en: Miki: "...yes."

rows.jp: 肩を落とす。

ghs.en: Shoulders drop.

rows.jp: 「理由は……霧ちんも言ってくれないんですけど、いつ頃からかそうなって」
rows.en: “She won’t tell me why... It just started somewhere along the way.”

ghs.en: Miki: "The reason... Kiri-chin never told me, but, it's been like this for some time."
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「うん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yep."

rows.jp: 「最近は、ちょっとノイローゼ気味っぽかったんですけど」
rows.en: “Lately she seemed almost obsessive about it.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Lately, she's felt a bit neurotic, however."

rows.jp: 「……そんな霧ちんと、うまくやっていけそうですか？」
rows.en: “...Do you think you can get along with her?”

ghs.en: Miki: "...can you get along with Kiri-chin when she's like this?"
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 不安そうに、美希は問いかけてきた。

ghs.en: So Miki asked, looking uneasy.

rows.jp: 「うん、俺が霧ちんとうまくやる約束で、曜子ちゃんから手を引いてもらったんで」
rows.en: “Yes. I promised Youko that Kiri-kins and I would get along, and she agreed to back off.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes, I promised to play nice with Kiri-chin, that's why I got Youko-chan to hold back."
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「支倉先輩って……先輩を傷つけると？」
rows.en: “Does Hasekura... come after anyone who hurts you?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Hasekura-senpai... did she hurt you, Senpai?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese status suffix remains untranslated, and the same sentence repeats its title as bare 'Senpai.'

rows.jp: 「どこからともなくあらわれる」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That one comes just out of nowhere, bam, no warning."

rows.jp: 「ヒーローみたいですね」

ghs.en: Miki: "Just like a hero, then."

rows.jp: 「そうだね。俺ヒロイン」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't that true. And me's heroine."
ghs.assessment: Taichi jokes that he is the heroine. The English uses an ungrammatical possessive construction and fails to state that equation.

rows.jp: 「女顔してます」

ghs.en: Miki: "Your face does look girly!"

rows.jp: 「……これでいい目見たこと一度もないです」
rows.en: “...It has never done me a lick of good.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...that I've never seen as something lucky not once."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says his feminine face has never once done him any good. The English is an ungrammatical relative fragment and does not convey that lack of benefit.

highlights.text: that I've never seen as something lucky not once

rows.jp: 「怯えられたり押し倒されたり混乱されたり」
rows.en: “People either get scared of me, pin me down, or just don't know what to make of me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I get frightened and I get pushed down and I get all confused."
ghs.assessment: Other people are frightened by him or confused, while he is knocked down. The English assigns all three reactions to Taichi himself.

highlights.text: I get frightened and I get pushed down and I get all confused

rows.jp: 「……そんなもんすか」

ghs.en: Miki: "...is that what it is?"

rows.jp: 「いっとき、人に会いたくなくなった。人と会話するのがいやだった」
rows.en: “For a while, I didn’t want to see anyone. I hated talking to people.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For a time, I didn't want to meet with anyone. I disliked conversing with people."

rows.jp: 「今は全然反対ですけど」

ghs.en: Miki: "Now it's totally the opposite however."

rows.jp: 「糧だから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because it's provisions."
ghs.assessment: 糧 is sustenance or nourishment in the figurative comparison. 'Provisions' suggests a stock of supplies rather than something psychologically necessary.

rows.jp: 「はい？」

ghs.en: Miki: "What?"

rows.jp: 「……必要なものだからな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...because it's something necessary."

rows.jp: 「食い物が嫌いだけど食わないと死ぬって状況」
rows.en: “It’s like hating food even though you’ll die if you don’t eat.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You might hate the food but if you don't eat, thing is, you'll be dying."
ghs.assessment: The construction is ungrammatical, and the general consequence 'you die' is changed into a future progressive event.

highlights.text: if you don't eat, thing is, you'll be dying

rows.jp: 「心の中でいろいろありまして、食う方に流れたわけだ」
rows.en: “A lot happened inside my head, and in the end I chose to eat.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There's many things inside of the heart, and they flow there based on the ways you eat."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that various things happened in his heart and he consequently came down on the side of eating. The English makes plural things flow somewhere according to methods of eating.

highlights.text: There's many things inside of the heart, and they flow there based on the ways you eat

rows.jp: 「人が俺に対してよからぬことを考えるのは、顔のせいだと思った。わけもわからず気になったのは、目だな」
rows.en: “I figured people got the wrong ideas about me because of my face. It was my eyes that bothered me, though, and I never knew why.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I thought that it was the face to blame for why people don't think good of me. And I don't understand why, but my eyes keep bothering me."
ghs.assessment: People don't think good of me is unidiomatic and recasts people having untoward ideas about Taichi as merely holding a poor opinion of him. The following reference to his eyes is not a wrong-subject error: the next exchange explicitly confirms that Taichi is preoccupied with how his own eyes differ from other people's.
ghs.remedy: Render the first relation as people getting the wrong idea about him because of his face; retain his own eyes as the object of his unexplained concern.

highlights.text: people don't think good of me

ghs.en: Miki: "Eyes?"

rows.jp: 「目が他人と違う気がして……いや、顔の造作も普通じゃないような気がして……」
rows.en: “They didn't seem like other people's eyes... No, I started thinking there was something wrong with my whole face...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It feels like my eyes are different from that of others... no, it also feels like my facial features aren't normal..."
ghs.assessment: The plural 'eyes' cannot be compared with the singular pronoun 'that'; the number must agree.

highlights.text: my eyes are different from that of others

rows.jp: 「小ぎれいですよ。いわゆるハンサムではないですが」

ghs.en: Miki: "They're trim and pretty. Not what you would call 'handsome' however."
ghs.assessment: Miki describes Taichi's face as neat or pretty. The plural pronoun instead points back to his eyes.

rows.jp: 「皆、そう言ってくれるけどね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That's just what everybody tells me."

rows.jp: 「ははあ、ソレが先輩の心の傷ってやつですか」
rows.en: “Aha. So that's your deep psychological wound?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Hah-ah... is that the wound on your heart, Senpai?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「んー、こんなのはオマケのオマケみたいなもので、本当は……」
rows.en: “No, this barely even counts—it’s an extra on top of an extra. The real thing is...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mmmmh, this is sort of the cherry on top of the cherry on top, in truth..."
ghs.assessment: オマケのオマケ calls this a mere extra on top of an extra, minimizing its importance. 'Cherry on top' normally presents a positive culminating bonus and reverses that force.

highlights.text: the cherry on top of the cherry on top

rows.jp: こらこら、と自分を諫める。

ghs.en: Come on!, come on!, I remonstrate myself.
ghs.assessment: The verb requires 'with' before its object in this sense, and the source is simply self-admonition.

rows.jp: 「とにかく取り引きなんで、曜子ちゃんに手を引いてもらうために霧は無力でいなければならないわけです」
rows.en: “In any case, this is a bargain. To make Youko withdraw, Kiri has to remain powerless.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, on to proper business. For purposes of getting Youko-chan to withdraw, it is absolutely imperative that Kiri remain free of offensive power."
ghs.assessment: とにかく取り引きなんで means that this is, in any case, a deal or bargain. The English instead announces a transition to business and retains a Japanese diminutive address later in the sentence.

rows.jp: 「話飛びーの」
rows.en: “And there he goes, vaulting clear over the topic.”

ghs.en: Miki: "The conversation's so juuumpy."

rows.jp: 「ということで霧ちん借ります」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And therefore, I shall be borrowing Kiri-chin."
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 「あのう……いじめないでやってくださいね？　いじりがいはあると思いますが」
rows.en: “Um... Please don't bully her. I know she's incredibly fun to mess with.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Ah, uhm... please don't tease her OK? I do think she's fun to tease, but..."

rows.jp: 「……善処します」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I will use my discretion."

rows.jp: 「なら、わたしもつきあいます」

ghs.en: Miki: "In that case I will be joining in, too."

rows.jp: こうして。

ghs.en: And this,

rows.jp: 美希も加わることになった。
rows.en: That was how Miki got drafted too.

ghs.en: was how Miki also joined us.
